NetDocuments is committed to providing an excellent candidate experience and will never ask you to engage in recruitment activity without phone, video, and in person meetings and communications from emails using the @netdocuments.com domain. If you have any concerns or questions about communications you have received, please send them to hrgroup@netdocuments.com so our team members can review.

About NetDocuments

At NetDocuments, we're shaping the future of legal work. We believe legal professionals should spend less time searching for information and managing documents, and more time solving complex problems, serving clients, and delivering meaningful outcomes. That's why we're building technology that helps organizations work smarter, collaborate more effectively, and unlock the full value of their institutional knowledge.

Our team is redefining what's possible for legal technology. NetDocuments is the trusted intelligent document management platform for legal professionals and the company behind the industry's first and only legal context graph—a breakthrough that gives legal professionals and AI a richer understanding of how matters, documents, people, and knowledge connect across an organization while respecting enterprise-grade security, governance, permissions, and ethical walls.

Innovation is only part of our story. We believe our greatest strength is our people. We foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing culture where curiosity is encouraged, diverse perspectives are valued, and employees are empowered to make a meaningful impact. Whether you're building products, serving customers, or supporting the business, your work helps shape the future of one of the world's most trusted legal technology platforms.

That commitment to our employees and customers has earned us recognition as one of the nation's top workplaces, including:

  • Four consecutive appearances on the Inc. 5000 list of America's Fastest-Growing Private Companies
  • Five-time Top Workplace USA winner
  • Five-time Salt Lake Tribune Top Workplace
  • Multiple Top Workplaces Culture Excellence awards recognizing innovation, employee appreciation, work-life flexibility, and compensation & benefits

If you're excited to solve meaningful challenges, work alongside talented colleagues, and help define the next generation of legal technology, we'd love to meet you.

What You’ll Do

NetDocuments is seeking a Principal Software Engineer – Intelligent DMS to provide technical leadership across the next generation of our document management platform. This role will help shape the architecture connecting our new web and mobile experiences, design system, extended applications, Microsoft 365 integrations, desktop applications, and AI-powered capabilities into a cohesive platform. You’ll operate as a deeply hands-on technical leader, spending the majority of your time solving complex engineering problems while driving architectural decisions that span multiple teams and products. You’ll partner closely with Product, Design, platform engineering, and our AI teams to establish scalable patterns, simplify complex systems, and ensure the experiences we build meet the reliability, security, performance, and usability standards expected by the world’s leading legal organizations.

You will:

Technical Leadership & Architecture

  • Provide technical leadership across the Intelligent DMS organization, establishing architectural direction and engineering standards that span multiple teams and product surfaces.
  • Lead architectural decisions across web, mobile, backend services, Microsoft 365 integrations, desktop applications, and AI-powered experiences.
  • Define shared technical patterns, component contracts, data models, permission models, and integration approaches that create a cohesive platform.
  • Lead complex, cross-team engineering initiatives from early product ideation through architecture, implementation, and production.
  • Evaluate architectural trade-offs across scalability, security, performance, usability, maintainability, and speed of delivery.
  • Simplify complex systems and establish technical foundations that enable teams to move faster as the platform evolves.

Design & Build

  • Contribute directly to the most complex and consequential areas of the Intelligent DMS platform.
  • Design and build cloud-native applications, microservices, integrations, and customer-facing experiences at enterprise scale.
  • Help architect the next-generation web and mobile applications and the backend services that support them.
  • Establish patterns for integrating AI capabilities such as assistants, summarization, extraction, and intelligent search into everyday document workflows.
  • Lead technical design for Microsoft 365 experiences, including co-authoring and integrations across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
  • Design solutions that maintain correctness, security, and matter-levl permissions across highly concurrent and distributed workflows.

Platform Evolution & Modernization

  • Define technical strategies for evolving mature applications and integrations onto the next-generation platform without disrupting critical customer workflows.
  • Establish migration patterns that allow legacy and next-generation experiences to operate effectively during platform transitions.
  • Drive technical coherence across extended applications, desktop clients, sync, import, browser extensions, mobile applications, and Microsoft 365 integrations.
  • Partner with platform and AI engineering teams to establish scalable integration patterns for shared services and capabilities.
  • Set performance and reliability standards for customer-facing applications and drive systemic improvements required to meet them.

Cross-Team Technical Leadership

  • Lead technical initiatives involving multiple engineering teams without relying on formal reporting authority.
  • Build alignment across Engineering, Product, Design, Platform, and AI teams around architectural direction and implementation strategy.
  • Translate ambiguous product opportunities into clear technical requirements, architecture, and executable plans.
  • Document architectural decisions and ensure teams understand the reasoning, trade-offs, and standards behind them.
  • Serve as a technical escalation point when teams encounter complex architectural or engineering challenges.

Engineering Excellence & Mentorship

  • Mentor engineers across experience levels, including Senior and Staff Engineers, and provide guidance on architecture, system design, and engineering practices.
  • Drive testing, quality, security, and reliability strategies across the Intelligent DMS organization.
  • Establish and maintain architecture documentation, engineering standards, and technical patterns that scale beyond individual projects.
  • Lead design and code reviews for complex or high-impact initiatives.
  • Partner with other Principal Engineers and our Chief Architect to advance technical excellence across the broader engineering organization.
  • Support recruiting and interviewing efforts to help build a high-performing engineering team.

Continuous Learning & Innovation

  • Stay current with advancements in AI-native product development, distributed systems, cloud architecture, and modern software engineering.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies and determine where they can meaningfully improve customer experience or engineering effectiveness.
  • Validate new technical approaches with real users and production feedback before scaling them broadly.
  • Champion engineering practices that prioritize simplicity, measurable customer value, and sustainable technical foundations.

What You’ll Need to Be Successful

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, with demonstrated experience operating at the Staff level or above.
  • Proven experience setting architecture and technical direction across multiple products, systems, or engineering teams.
  • Experience leading complex, cross-team technical initiatives without formal authority and driving alignment across engineering stakeholders.
  • Deep expertise in system design, distributed systems, cloud applications, microservices, and enterprise-scale integrations.
  • Strong full stack engineering experience with the ability to work across frontend and backend systems; our technology stack includes C#, .NET, React, and TypeScript.
  • Experience designing and operating cloud-native systems using AWS, Azure, or comparable cloud technologies.
  • Experience translating ambiguous product requirements into clear technical architecture and implementation plans.
  • Demonstrated experience mentoring senior engineers and providing technical guidance across teams.
  • Strong technical writing skills with experience creating architecture documents, design proposals, and technical decision records.

What Will Make You Stand Out

  • Experience shipping AI-native product experiences where AI is fundamental to the product workflow.
  • Experience operating multi-tenant enterprise platforms with strict security, compliance, or data residency requirements.
  • Experience with Microsoft 365 extensibility, including Office add-ins, Microsoft Graph, or co-authoring technologies.
  • Experience modernizing legacy applications while maintaining heavily used production systems and managing complex customer migrations.
  • Experience in legal technology, professional-services SaaS, or other regulated enterprise software environments.
  • Public examples of technical leadership through conference speaking, technical writing, open-source contributions, or architectural patterns adopted by other teams.
  • A track record of leading complex technical initiatives through both successful outcomes and lessons learned from approaches that did not work.

What You’ll Love About NetDocuments

  • The People!
  • 90% healthcare premiums company covered
  • HSA company contribution
  • 401(k) match at 4% with immediate vesting
  • Flexible PTO (typically 3 to 4 weeks a year)
  • 10 paid holidays
  • Monthly contributions for life activities & wellness
  • Access to LinkedIn Learning with monthly dedicated time to explore
  • Connection, access, and mentorship from exceptional leaders
  • Growing company with opportunities for advancement
  • Authenticity and accountability from leadership

Compensation Transparency

The compensation range for this position is $200,000 – $220,000.

The posted cash compensation includes on-target earnings. Some roles may qualify for overtime pay. Individual compensation packages are determined based on factors such as experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location.

Equal Opportunity

NetDocuments is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, (including pregnancy), national origin, age, physical and mental disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, military and veteran status, or any other status protected by laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. NetDocuments believes diversity and inclusion among our employees is critical to our success, and we are committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment.

title: Overhead Line (OHL) Design engineer
description: Power Networks provides high quality consultancy services within distribution network (cable and overhead lines) and transmission (cable). We support our clients throughout every stage of the process — from early feasibility studies to design, execution, and project management. Our expertise also includes market, regulatory, and environmental analysis. Today, our work spans overhead lines and underground cables. At Power Networks, we are approximately 30 employees located across our offices in Stockholm, Göteborg, Skellefteå, Linköping, Karlstad, Uppsala, Karlskrona, Kalmar and Jönköping. As an Overhead Line (OHL) Design engineer at WSP , you will experience a great variety in your work, engaging in projects for multiple clients and network owners. Typical projects involve design, construction, and calculations within the overhead line segment, covering voltage levels from 30 kV to 130 kV. Some of your responsibilies will include: Lead or contribute to overhead line design for medium voltage grids. Perform tower spotting, line profiling, and routing studies. Conduct sag and tension calculations according to international or Scandinavian standards. Coordinate with Swedish internal teams. Ensure technical compliance, quality, and design optimization. The team works together closely to achieve project goals while continuously sharing knowledge and experience to foster growth. At WSP, we offer exciting opportunities to work on a diverse range of overhead line projects, both big and small. You have the flexibility to focus on what drives you and supports your professional development. With colleagues spread across Sweden, you will collaborate with highly skilled professionals in various specialties. We strongly encourage close teamwork, even when working remotely. In this role you can be placed at any of WSP’s offices in Sweden or where WSP has offices globally. To succeed in this role, we believe that you have: Bachelor’s degree (minimum) in Electrical, Civil, or Mechanical Engineering. At least three years experience in overhead power line design (33–130 kV). Strong competence in tower spotting or sag/tension calculations. Familiarity with PLS-CADD or similar design tools is a strong advantage. Prior experience working on European or Scandinavian utility projects is a plus. Knowledge of AutoCAD or Microstation. If you have experience in Icetow, AvCAD or similar programs, it is a merit. Previous experience working as a consultant is also considered a plus. Additionally, we consider it a merit if you have familiarity with AMA standards, construction, and workplace safety regulations. We operate in an international environment, so it is important that you are comfortable communicating in English. Swedish is a merit. Contact Omobobola Adetunji People Lead Power Networks, Omobobola.adetunji@wsp.com Sofie Grettve, Senior Talent Acquisition Specialist, sofie.grettve@wsp.com Don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any questions! Application deadline Selection is ongoing, but we would like to receive your application no later than 15th of June.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Product Engineering, EU
description: Hi I’m Abhik , Ashby 's Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. We’re looking for an ambitious full-stack engineer who is laser-focused on solving customer problems and making the right long-term investments to solve them not only today but in our future features and products. What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense of a seed startup: you write product specs, make product and design decisions, and build in an almost-no-meeting culture. While also the product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: tens of thousands of daily users who depend on your software and eagerly await your next feature. We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. You’ve probably seen this role posted before, and it’s because we’re always expanding the team (we’re on track to double this year). We’re bubbling with ideas on how to support Talent Acquisition through software, and we’ve started the journey of building products beyond Talent Acquisition. We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner). About the Role and How We Work Our engineering culture strives to recreate the environments where we did our best work as ICs – where we had the ownership and agency to impact our users with creative and innovative software. I started my career building software for artists in the Visual Effects industry. It was a formative experience for me as a software engineer because success relied on my ability to be a product manager and designer. I talked to artists to understand their needs. I came up with ideas. I did industry research, designed interfaces, and prototyped ideas. I watched artists use what I built and decided what to tackle in the next iteration. No daily stand-ups, no t-shirt sizing, no planning meetings. I studied computer science to solve problems, not tickets, and this felt exactly like that. I not only felt creative and fulfilled but the agency and ownership we were given as engineers powered an incredible amount of innovation. Innovation came differently (or not at all) at technology startups beyond the seed stage, often through an engineer’s force of will and ability to push back against culture (rather than any encouragement from it). Engineering was narrowed to implementation and delivery, partly due to the influence of other departments and partly due to the influx of "Agile" processes like sprint planning. In those companies, I felt like a JIRA jockey. At Ashby, we’re building an environment that is optimistic about what engineers can own and achieve. An environment that embraces innovative engineers, and, frankly, often stays out of their way. As a Product Engineer, you’ll take ownership over a large portion of one of our products and own projects end-to-end (wearing hats traditionally worn by product and design). You’ll research competitors, write product specs, make wireframes, and more. To ground it with examples, product engineers at Ashby have: Designed and built automated interview scheduling. This feature automates scheduling by calculating possible times from a pool of interviewers and other constraints, and then presenting these times to the candidate for selection via our responsive web app. This solves the “Calendar Tetris” problem I talk about in "What We're Building." Built a generalized declarative filter architecture that allows users to create complex filters for any record with a consistent UI and compile it to SQL in our backend. Many user-facing features use it. Specced, designed, and implemented a feature that allows users to complete signing offers entirely within Ashby. This project involved talking to customers to understand their requirements, deciding what technologies to use, building a prototype, and working with other team members to integrate the final implementation into additional features. What We’re Building As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back. Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. TA software didn’t help. As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are! Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply Software engineers come in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. Here are some things to help you decide if this fits you and what you’re looking for: You’re not afraid to tackle any part of a technology stack. You do what’s necessary to successfully deliver a feature, whether writing frontend or choosing new infrastructure. We’ll provide a supportive environment to do it successfully (e.g., design system, SRE team). You’ve tackled projects with a lot of product and technical ambiguity, and you thrive at the intersection of the two. We’re not building a simple CRUD app, and many of the challenges we tackle require you to use your knowledge of our customers to build powerful abstractions and flexibility in the system to solve a class of problems. You know how to strike the right balance between speed and quality. Ashby wasn’t built quickly. We took four years to launch publicly because convincing customers to switch required a high-quality product. However, time isn’t infinite, especially for a startup, so we still move with urgency—we’ve built the equivalent of three or more VC-backed startups with a very small team. You are ambitious and always looking to improve your skills. For most engineers, this role will give you more freedom and responsibilities than you’ve experienced in the past. To thrive (and level up), you’ll need to be open to feedback (and we give lots of it). You’re an excellent collaborator and communicator. Ownership and freedom don’t mean you work in a vacuum. You’ll need to vet your decisions with the appropriate stakeholders, keep them up to date when necessary, and work with other engineers to get your projects across the finish line. Clear and concise communication helps a lot here! You seek to create leverage in your work. The nature of software is that you can often automate or abstract what would be tedious, time-consuming work. Your impatience usually leads to new abstractions, tools to allow Support to debug before Engineering, new lint rules to prevent common bugs, etc. Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if: You need company-driven process and structure to get your projects across the finish line. Sprint planning and well-defined project management processes are things you need or look to others to lead. You’d rather focus on the technical details and challenges. You only want to do exciting work. We’re building a team of kind, collaborative folks. Customer issues and investigations are distributed across the team, including our high-level ICs. You can get lost in the details. Once you start implementation, it can be hard to take a step back and think about the project as a whole. You like everything to be planned upfront. You haven’t led or taken ownership of projects before. You’re used to working with tech leads and taking on tasks distributed by them. You want to mentor earlier-career engineers. We rely on engineers owning their projects, so we need engineers with that experience. This requires the team to be reasonably tenured. More than 90% of the team would be considered Senior or above in the industry today, so mentorship opportunities are very limited. To you, a tech lead, staff, or principal engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or doing architecture reviews. Our most tenured engineers spend most of their time building, and we often trust them with our most challenging problems. While they lead product and technical areas and help other engineers plan their most challenging work, it’s not a requirement, nor do engineers need their sign-off. Engineering Culture Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (my Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through: Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design Natural collaboration and deliberate communication Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage Putting effort into building a diverse team Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They took customer problems and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise. Traditional product-development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But, consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.” At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, at Ashby, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive . Collaboration is Natural & Communication is Deliberate Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here !). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here ). To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over 4 years: We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region. Increase Leverage, not Team Size We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in: Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 15x a day. A debugger that works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience . Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below). Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby: And a demo of one of these building blocks: Put Effort into Diversity Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups. Today, 21% of engineers at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. It’s not great, and we are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more. Interview Process At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together via pair programming, writing product and tech specs collaboratively, and talking through decisions. There are no leetcode or whiteboard exercises. Our interview process is three rounds: Introduction call with Hiring Manager (15 to 30m, live) A technical screen where we pair in our actual codebase (1h, live) Three non-coding interviews that focus on product thinking, technical design, and infrastructure (3h 15m, live can be split across multiple days) Depending on our leadership team’s bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter. Your hiring manager will be your main point of contact and prep you for interviews. Each round will have written guidance so you know what to expect (you’ll need minimal preparation). You’ll meet 4 to 6 people in engineering (with 5-15 minutes in each interview to ask them questions). If we don’t give an offer, we’ll provide feedback! Your First Three Months at Ashby We want an exceptional onboarding experience for every new hire. At Ashby, your dev environment is set up with a single script, you push your first product change on day one, and you spend the rest of your time shipping product changes that give you a tour of our codebase and best practices. The product changes increase in scope and ambiguity from simple copy changes to the delivery of a prominent, impactful feature. Your manager will do a 30, 60, and 90-day review to give feedback and calibrate on how we work together. It’s a team effort to get you successfully onboarded; you’ll have a peer paired with you to answer questions, pair program, and check in often to see if you need help. The rest of the team will run training sessions on our culture, product, engineering process, and technical architecture. Technology Stack I’m sharing our tech stack with the caveat that we don’t require previous experience in it (but a love of typed languages is helpful ): TypeScript (frontend & backend), React, GraphQL API, Node.js, Postgres, Redis. When they joined Ashby, many of our engineers switched from other languages like Swift and Kotlin ( Ben ), platforms like iOS ( Tom ) and Windows ( Sergey ). We care more about fundamentals (e.g., debugging, abstractions) and how fast you learn. For folks on the team who switched, it's nice seeing changes hot reload versus waiting for XCode to compile . Benefits Competitive salary and equity. 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it. A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements. Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive! $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval. If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us. Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply. Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

I came up with ideas. I did industry research, designed interfaces, and prototyped ideas. I watched artists use what I built and decided what to tackle in the next iteration. No daily stand-ups, no t-shirt sizing, no planning meetings.

I studied computer science to solve problems, not tickets, and this felt exactly like that. I not only felt creative and fulfilled but the agency and ownership we were given as engineers powered an incredible amount of innovation.

Innovation came differently (or not at all) at technology startups beyond the seed stage, often through an engineer’s force of will and ability to push back against culture (rather than any encouragement from it). Engineering was narrowed to implementation and delivery, partly due to the influence of other departments and partly due to the influx of "Agile" processes like sprint planning. In those companies, I felt like a JIRA jockey.

At Ashby, we’re building an environment that is optimistic about what engineers can own and achieve. An environment that embraces innovative engineers, and, frankly, often stays out of their way. As a Product Engineer, you’ll take ownership over a large portion of one of our products and own projects end-to-end (wearing hats traditionally worn by product and design). You’ll research competitors, write product specs, make wireframes, and more. To ground it with examples, product engineers at Ashby have:

  • Designed and built automated interview scheduling. This feature automates scheduling by calculating possible times from a pool of interviewers and other constraints, and then presenting these times to the candidate for selection via our responsive web app. This solves the “Calendar Tetris” problem I talk about in "What We're Building."

  • Built a generalized declarative filter architecture that allows users to create complex filters for any record with a consistent UI and compile it to SQL in our backend. Many user-facing features use it.

  • Specced, designed, and implemented a feature that allows users to complete signing offers entirely within Ashby. This project involved talking to customers to understand their requirements, deciding what technologies to use, building a prototype, and working with other team members to integrate the final implementation into additional features.

What We’re Building

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply

Software engineers come in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. Here are some things to help you decide if this fits you and what you’re looking for:

  • You’re not afraid to tackle any part of a technology stack. You do what’s necessary to successfully deliver a feature, whether writing frontend or choosing new infrastructure. We’ll provide a supportive environment to do it successfully (e.g., design system, SRE team).

  • You’ve tackled projects with a lot of product and technical ambiguity, and you thrive at the intersection of the two. We’re not building a simple CRUD app, and many of the challenges we tackle require you to use your knowledge of our customers to build powerful abstractions and flexibility in the system to solve a class of problems.

  • You know how to strike the right balance between speed and quality. Ashby wasn’t built quickly. We took four years to launch publicly because convincing customers to switch required a high-quality product. However, time isn’t infinite, especially for a startup, so we still move with urgency—we’ve built the equivalent of three or more VC-backed startups with a very small team.

  • You are ambitious and always looking to improve your skills. For most engineers, this role will give you more freedom and responsibilities than you’ve experienced in the past. To thrive (and level up), you’ll need to be open to feedback (and we give lots of it).

  • You’re an excellent collaborator and communicator. Ownership and freedom don’t mean you work in a vacuum. You’ll need to vet your decisions with the appropriate stakeholders, keep them up to date when necessary, and work with other engineers to get your projects across the finish line. Clear and concise communication helps a lot here!

  • You seek to create leverage in your work. The nature of software is that you can often automate or abstract what would be tedious, time-consuming work. Your impatience usually leads to new abstractions, tools to allow Support to debug before Engineering, new lint rules to prevent common bugs, etc.

Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if:

  • You need company-driven process and structure to get your projects across the finish line. Sprint planning and well-defined project management processes are things you need or look to others to lead. You’d rather focus on the technical details and challenges.

  • You only want to do exciting work. We’re building a team of kind, collaborative folks. Customer issues and investigations are distributed across the team, including our high-level ICs.

  • You can get lost in the details. Once you start implementation, it can be hard to take a step back and think about the project as a whole. You like everything to be planned upfront.

  • You haven’t led or taken ownership of projects before. You’re used to working with tech leads and taking on tasks distributed by them.

  • You want to mentor earlier-career engineers. We rely on engineers owning their projects, so we need engineers with that experience. This requires the team to be reasonably tenured. More than 90% of the team would be considered Senior or above in the industry today, so mentorship opportunities are very limited.

  • To you, a tech lead, staff, or principal engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or doing architecture reviews. Our most tenured engineers spend most of their time building, and we often trust them with our most challenging problems. While they lead product and technical areas and help other engineers plan their most challenging work, it’s not a requirement, nor do engineers need their sign-off.

Engineering Culture

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (my Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

  • Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

  • Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

  • Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage

  • Putting effort into building a diverse team

Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They took customer problems and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional product-development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But, consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, at Ashby, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

Collaboration is Natural & Communication is Deliberate

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here).

To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over 4 years:

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

Increase Leverage, not Team Size

We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:

  • Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 15x a day. A debugger that works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience .

  • Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:

And a demo of one of these building blocks:

Put Effort into Diversity

Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.

Today, 21% of engineers at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. It’s not great, and we are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

Interview Process

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together via pair programming, writing product and tech specs collaboratively, and talking through decisions. There are no leetcode or whiteboard exercises.

Our interview process is three rounds:

  1. Introduction call with Hiring Manager (15 to 30m, live)

  2. A technical screen where we pair in our actual codebase (1h, live)

  3. Three non-coding interviews that focus on product thinking, technical design, and infrastructure (3h 15m, live can be split across multiple days)

Depending on our leadership team’s bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter.

Your hiring manager will be your main point of contact and prep you for interviews. Each round will have written guidance so you know what to expect (you’ll need minimal preparation). You’ll meet 4 to 6 people in engineering (with 5-15 minutes in each interview to ask them questions). If we don’t give an offer, we’ll provide feedback!

Your First Three Months at Ashby

We want an exceptional onboarding experience for every new hire. At Ashby, your dev environment is set up with a single script, you push your first product change on day one, and you spend the rest of your time shipping product changes that give you a tour of our codebase and best practices. The product changes increase in scope and ambiguity from simple copy changes to the delivery of a prominent, impactful feature. Your manager will do a 30, 60, and 90-day review to give feedback and calibrate on how we work together.

It’s a team effort to get you successfully onboarded; you’ll have a peer paired with you to answer questions, pair program, and check in often to see if you need help. The rest of the team will run training sessions on our culture, product, engineering process, and technical architecture.

Technology Stack

I’m sharing our tech stack with the caveat that we don’t require previous experience in it (but a love of typed languages is helpful ): TypeScript (frontend & backend), React, GraphQL API, Node.js, Postgres, Redis.

When they joined Ashby, many of our engineers switched from other languages like Swift and Kotlin (Ben), platforms like iOS (Tom) and Windows (Sergey). We care more about fundamentals (e.g., debugging, abstractions) and how fast you learn. For folks on the team who switched, it's nice seeing changes hot reload versus waiting for XCode to compile .

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

  • A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

For us it is also important that we make an impact on our employees, that they feel challenged and ease. We consist of a rapid growing and ambitious team with all different backgrounds. Entrepreneurs, Operational specialists, Developers, Sales gurus you can find them all at Workwize and are always on the look-out for the next original ideas to reach more consumers and create the best value for our customers. We are looking forward to meeting you and discover if there is a match with the Workwize team! Please note: For this role we are not offering relocation support or visa sponsorship.

Our Justride platform is used in over 250 locations globally, including some of the largest cities in the world. raw.jobDescription:
About Us_
// At Masabi, we’re driving the fare payment revolution, powering the journeys of millions all over the world. We build fare collection platforms that allow riders to seamlessly buy and present tickets for public transport either on their mobile phones, from a ticket machine, or even by tapping their bank card to travel.

Our Justride platform is used in over 250 locations globally, including some of the largest cities in the world. With our industry-first mobile ticketing SDK, we’ve partnered with large players in the transport space, including Uber, Moovit and Transit.

Your own journey is important to us too. Choosing a role here means joining a network of innovators from all walks of life; a group of passionate individuals who consistently deliver. Here, you’ll find the tools you need to build the career you want. Whether you’re taking the direct route or trying a new path, we’ll support you no matter what.

The Role_

// We’re looking for a Principal Engineer - Payments to join Masabi’s Architecture team, with a primary focus on our payments domain.

This is a senior role for someone who combines strong technical judgement with deep payments experience. You’ll shape the technical direction of our payments platform while staying close enough to the detail to design, review and support meaningful technical work.

Working across the engineering organisation, you’ll act as a senior technical leader within the payments domain: contributing to architecture, guiding complex decisions and helping teams build scalable, resilient systems that support millions of journeys worldwide.

The role suits someone who can move between system-level thinking and implementation, who understands trade-offs, can navigate ambiguity and helps turn complex or loosely defined problems into clear, practical technical approaches.

Location_

// This role is open to candidates based anywhere in the UK, with the flexibility to work fully remotely. For those based in or around London, we also offer the option of hybrid working from our London office.



Responsibilities_

  • Shape the technical direction of Masabi’s payments platform, contributing to architecture, standards and engineering best practices

  • Design and deliver scalable, secure, resilient and cost-effective payment solutions aligned with Masabi’s platform direction

  • Support teams in building towards a modern, microservices-based architecture while balancing delivery priorities and long-term platform health

  • Stay close to technical delivery through architecture reviews, design discussions and targeted hands-on contribution where needed

  • Identify and work through complex technical challenges related to scalability, resilience, operational performance and system evolution

  • Act as a senior technical advisor across engineering teams, supporting and influencing technical decisions, particularly within the payments domain

  • Work with external providers and payment partners on integrations, technical alignment and problem-solving

  • Contribute to technical roadmap planning, prioritisation, technical scoping and architecture discussions for complex initiatives

  • Produce clear technical documentation and contribute to engineering standards, technical forums and good practices across the organisation

About You_

// You bring a mix of strong technical expertise, sound judgement and real-world payments experience.

  • Strong experience working on payment systems, including integrations with PSPs, gateways, EMV, contactless EMV, acquirers, etc.

  • Good understanding of payment flows, transaction lifecycles and system design considerations

  • Experience designing and evolving distributed systems and microservices architectures

  • You’ve operated at Principal or Staff level, shaping technical direction across multiple teams or domains

  • Strong judgement and the ability to balance short-term delivery with long-term architectural outcomes

  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity and turning complex problems into clear, practical technical approaches

  • Clear and thoughtful communicator, able to engage both technical and non-technical audiences

  • Comfortable being hands-on where needed, while maintaining a focus on system-level impact

  • You have strong experience with cloud platforms (AWS preferred) and modern infrastructure practices

  • You’ve worked on systems where scale, reliability, performance and cost trade-offs matter, and can navigate those decisions thoughtfully

  • You’ve contributed to engineering standards, architecture patterns or platform direction

About Enode

The grid was built for predictable, centralised power. Today it's absorbing intermittent supply from grid scale solar and wind, alongside dynamic demand from EVs, heat pumps, and home batteries. The missing piece is software that can connect and orchestrate these devices at scale.

Enode provides the infrastructure layer that makes this possible. Our Connect API gives energy companies a single integration to 1000+ devices across 80+ brands. Our optimisation tooling gives energy companies the building blocks to manage those devices locally - think smart charging for EVs. Our Flex product turns those connected devices into a flexible, controllable asset for energy companies.

We work with device manufacturers across the energy hardware ecosystem - from EV brands to heat pump and solar inverter producers. Our customers are energy retailers, utilities, and traders building the next generation of energy services. We're backed by Y Combinator, Lowercarbon Capital, and Creandum.

The decisions made now will shape how the energy system gets built. We're looking for people who take ownership, move fast, and care deeply about the role technology can play in the energy transition.

What we're looking for:

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to help build the software layer that makes home energy devices work as one system. The Home Energy team owns Enode's integrations and APIs for batteries, solar inverters, HVAC, and smart meters, along with the home energy management (HEM) system and statistics that customers build on. You'll build integrations with leading OEMs and help mature our API surface into the unified control layer for the home, at a moment when customer demand for battery and home energy optimization is accelerating.

You'll join the Home Energy team, reporting to the team's Engineering Manager. You'll collaborate closely with your PM, fellow backend engineers, and our partnership and commercial teams, from assessing OEM API feasibility to shaping how customers control energy assets through our platform.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and maintain integrations with OEM cloud platforms across batteries, solar, smart meters, and HVAC.

  • Design and evolve our home energy APIs, unifying telemetry and controls across HEM system, batteries, and curtailment into a product surface customers can build optimizations on.

  • Improve observability and vendor performance across our integrations, and take part in the team's triage rotation.

  • Work with partnership and commercial teams on API feasibility for new OEM integrations.

  • Take a product-engineer mindset, balancing speed, quality, and customer impact in your day-to-day decisions.

Curious what you'd actually be building? Explore our API docs and the Enode Tech Blog to see what we ship and how we think about it.

This role will be right for you, if:

You're an ambitious backend engineer who likes to own things end to end: from an ambiguous problem, through design and integration work, to something shipped and running in production. You find integration challenges satisfying rather than frustrating, including working with third-party APIs of varying maturity, and you're energized by tough technical problems.

You're comfortable navigating ambiguity and bringing clarity and structure that help a team move forward. You collaborate naturally with engineers, PMs, and commercial partners, and you like being close enough to the product to influence where it goes.

  • Experience with TypeScript/Node, AWS services, PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB, or similar production tooling.

  • Familiarity with home energy assets (batteries, solar/inverters, HVAC, smart meters), energy markets, or IoT/device ecosystems.

title: Director, EMEA Ocean Operations
description:
About Flexport: 

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year. 

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

About the role: 

Your responsibilities as a Director, EMEA Ocean Operations include, but are not limited to the following:

  • Lead and develop a leadership team of Senior Managers and Managers, who in turn run Ocean Operations teams across EMEA. You are accountable for organisation design, hiring plans and succession planning at every level beneath you. You build a culture of high performance and psychological safety, and you make sure the organisation scales with the business rather than just adding people.
  • Own end-to-end EMEA ocean gateway operations (FCL and LCL) across all markets, both insourced and partner-operated countries. You set one operating standard for how work is done, and you decide where it makes sense for local markets to differ.
  • Define and deliver the multi-year EMEA ocean strategy and the planning cycles that support it (biannual planning and quarterly check-ins). You separate what the core operation needs to keep running well from what is expansion, and you turn that into clear choices on investment, team size and priorities, aligned with EMEA operations goals.
  • Build and drive the EMEA ocean automation roadmap with your teams. You decide where to remove manual work first, so that volume growth does not need proportional growth in manual work, and you work with Product, Engineering and Operational Excellence to deliver it.
  • Act as the senior operations voice to EMEA Operational Excellence, Global Product and Engineering. You turn operational pain points across EMEA into clear product priorities, and you help decide what gets built.
  • Report to the EMEA Head of Operations and serve as a member of the EMEA Senior Leadership Team. You help set the direction for EMEA as a whole, not just for your own area.
  • Partner with EMEA commercial leadership (GMs) and global operations leaders in other regions. You make sure commercial promises and operational reality match, you flag deal and delivery risk early, and you share what works across regions.
  • Hold executive-level relationships with key clients, carriers and partner operators. You lead major escalations, negotiate service commitments with partners, and represent EMEA operations in client business reviews.
  • Use data to find the biggest bottlenecks and root causes across markets, not just fix individual cases. You set the metrics the organisation runs on and make sure leaders at every level are held to them in regular reviews (weekly, monthly and quarterly business reviews).
  • Own the long-term capacity plan. You work with Operations Excellence and Finance on staffing models that cope with seasonal peaks and multi-year growth, including the balance between insourced teams and partners.
  • Own the P&L and operational health of EMEA ocean gateway operations. You set the financial discipline for your area, stop revenue and cost leakage at scale (for example, billing accessorials), and make sure your leaders do the same in their teams.

Prerequisites:

  • BA/BS degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management or equivalent experience
  • Proven track record of measurable business results, including quantified impact on quality, productivity, efficiency and customer service
  • 10+ years of experience in cross-border supply chains, logistics and/or freight forwarding, with ocean freight experience
  • 5+ years of people management experience, including managing managers
  • 3+ years in customer-facing roles, with experience managing senior client or partner relationships
  • Experience running operations across several countries
  • Technology (and AI) first mindset, comfortable in a fast-paced environment
  • Excellent English; ideally other European languages
  • Excellent technical skills (e.g. Claude, N8N, Looker, Excel)
  • Owner's mindset and strong discipline across the whole organisation
  • Customer obsession, with high standards as a point of pride
  • An operator at heart who removes waste and redesigns processes for lean, scalable efficiency
  • Dives into metrics to fix root causes while delivering the short-term wins that stabilise operations
  • Builds trust through transparent, concise communication and encourages the team to challenge the status quo

What's in it for you:

  • An opportunity to contribute to one of the fastest-growing companies, where you’ll have the chance to create a global impact while being a part of a  thriving multinational environment 
  • Daily catered lunches incl. vegetarian options, breakfast, snacks and soft drinks available in our office on daily basis 
  • Commute expenses: Flexport will cover  home-office commuting costs for employees living outside of Amsterdam
  • Amazing office in the heart of Amsterdam. 
  • 25 working days as vacation days based on full time employment.
  • Health insurance: Flexport offers a collective health insurance plan including a basic package and any available additional packages. Your monthly premium is fully paid by Flexport. 
  • A defined pension contribution scheme

title: Senior Embedded Performance Engineer
description:
Auterion builds a cutting-edge operating system for autonomous robotic systems that empower a diverse range of platforms to perform surveillance, reconnaissance, inspection, mapping and logistics tasks. Our industry-leading software drives the adoption of robotic fleets and is recognized by the U.S. government as the future standard for its drone programs. 

We are looking for a Senior Embedded Performance Engineer who is passionate about getting the most out of embedded systems — from low-level Linux tuning and hardware integration to high-performance video and data pipelines. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working close to hardware, moving across the stack, and solving the kinds of problems where milliseconds, bandwidth, startup time, and system efficiency matter.

You will work across the AuterionOS ecosystem on topics such as:

  • Embedded Linux performance and system tuning
  • Low-latency video streaming and media pipelines
  • C/C++, Python, and Bash-based platform development
  • Hardware integration, system profiling, and end-to-end optimization
  • Collaboration with experienced and driven engineers across Auterion

Responsibilities

  • Work within the Apps & Simulation team and collaborate with other development teams to build high-performance products for autonomous systems.
  • Design, optimize, and maintain performance-critical components within AuterionOS, Auterion’s custom embedded Linux distribution.
  • Improve end-to-end system behavior across compute, networking, video, and hardware interfaces, with a strong focus on latency, throughput, reliability, and resource efficiency.
  • Analyze and optimize demanding workloads such as real-time telemetry, video streaming, media processing, and communication between distributed system components.
  • Investigate system bottlenecks across the full stack, from kernel and OS behavior to application-level code and tooling.
  • Collaborate with engineering and product teams to understand both internal and customer use cases, and translate them into robust technical solutions.
  • Propose and implement new platform capabilities with a strong emphasis on measurable performance gains in real-world deployments.
  • Participate in daily stand-ups, release planning, and prioritization discussions.

Qualifications and Skills

  • B.Sc. or M.Sc. in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of professional experience writing object-oriented C++ and/or Python.
  • Deep experience with embedded Linux systems, including cross-compilation, debugging, profiling, and performance tuning.
  • Strong hands-on background in diagnosing and optimizing real-world system behavior, including CPU, memory, I/O, networking, boot time, and application latency.
  • Experience building or optimizing low-latency video or data-streaming pipelines, ideally on embedded platforms.
  • Excellent understanding of software systems that span embedded devices, higher-level applications, and fully integrated products.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, including system design, implementation, debugging, and testing.
  • Experience with video codecs, GStreamer, RTP/RTSP, or hardware-accelerated media pipelines.
  • Solid experience with Debian/Ubuntu-based systems, Bash scripting, and systemd.
  • Experience with Docker and docker-compose in complex development and deployment environments, as well as qemu.
  • Strong debugging and performance analysis skills at both system and application level, combined with a proactive and self-directed working style.
  • Proficient in ROS2/DDS-style middleware and experienced with networking across multiple OSI layers, including REST APIs and performance-sensitive communication paths.
  • Experience with system integration and interfacing sensors or peripherals, especially via USB and Ethernet.
  • Experience working in an agile engineering environment with stand-ups, sprint planning, and shared ownership across teams.
  • Bonus: Experience with build systems such as CMake, including improving build performance in large-scale software projects.

Benefits

  • Flexible working hours
  • Stock Options
  • Generous holiday allowance
  • Company pension plan 
  • Car parking  
  • Enhanced maternity & paternity leave
  • Mental health and wellbeing support
  • Learning and development opportunities

We are building the leading software platform for AI-powered autonomous systems for enterprise and government customers. Our team is supporting the most important missions and solving the most challenging problems.

At Auterion, we bring together the sharpest minds who love to solve the hardest problems. Join a vibrant team built on innovation, openness, and excellence, where you’ll be empowered to develop ideas, collaborate across all levels, and make an impact that matters.

title: Senior Projectmanager
description: Jouw Missie bij CCS Geen dag is hetzelfde in deze rol. Samen met je collega’s zorg je ervoor dat wij succesvol onze softwareoplossingen bij klanten implementeren en dat onze klanten een excellente dienstverlening krijgen! Voor deze complexe systeemimplementaties en integratieprojecten zoeken we een zeer ervaren projectmanager. Je leert de verzekeringsbranche kennen en klanten helpen. Dat doe je niet alleen: je werkt samen met enthousiaste collega’s in een projectteam. Voordelen voor de sollicitant Als projectmanager krijg je veel verantwoordelijkheid, help je klanten en samen met je projectteam zet je mooie resultaten neer. Je kunt deels thuiswerken, deels op ons kantoor in Woerden en bij verschillende klanten in Nederland. Tijdelijk werken vanuit het buitenland kan ook dankzij onze workation-regeling (maximaal 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar). Bij ons draait het om klantgericht werken én werkplezier. Daarom is er volop ruimte voor ontspanning en plezier. Denk aan een levend tafelvoetbaltoernooi, pubquiz en een bier- & wijnproeverij. Ons actieve Fun-team zorgt elke maand weer voor iets leuks. En als je reislust nog niet is gestild met 25 vakantiedagen en een workation, dan kun je zelfs tot 20 extra verlofdagen bijkopen. Genoeg redenen om verder te lezen en te ontdekken of deze functie iets voor jou is, toch? Een voorbeeld van je werkdag Opstarten: Aan het begin van je werkdag heb je een dagstart met zowel collega’s als projectteamleden van de klant. Hierin bespreken jullie de voortgang, resultaten en eventuele hulpvragen. Na de dagstart: Allereerst neem je nog wat tijd met een van de consultants naar aanleiding van de dagstart. Je coacht en begeleidt de consultant en helpt deze met een hulpvraag. Vervolgens ga je aan de slag met het opstellen van de voortgangsrapportage. Hiermee zorg je voor proactieve en transparante rapportage over het project aan de klant. De stuurgroep met de klant is volgende week, vandaag spreek je samen met de delivery manager deze stuurgroep voor. Wat zijn de belangrijkste punten voor de klant en voor CCS en hoe vliegen we die aan. Na de lunch: Je checkt nog een paar tickets qua voortgang op het planboard, waarbij je de samenhang met de planning checkt. Vervolgens ga je naar de werksessie met het CCS projectmanagement guild. Hier werken jullie aan tickets om de CCS Prince2Agile projectmethodiek verder te verbeteren. Hierna heb je nog een afspraak met je collega van sales voor afstemming over een mogelijk vervolgproject bij de klant. Wie jij bent De ideale kandidaat beschikt over daadkracht, doorzettingsvermogen, enthousiasme en drive om projecten succesvol te leiden en verbeteringen door te voeren om te komen tot nog efficiëntere en klantgerichte projecten. Jij herkent jezelf in de volgende punten: · Je wordt blij van projectmanagement en blijft kalm bij verschuivende prioriteiten; · Je hebt bewezen ervaring met het succesvol uitvoeren van productsoftware-implementaties in een complexe, maar klantgerichte omgeving, binnen budget, planning en scope; · Je hebt ruime ervaring met diverse projectmanagement en delivery methodieken, bij voorkeur een Prince2-, Ipma of PMI of Agile / scrum certificaat; · Je vindt, net als wij, klanttevredenheid het uitgangspunt. Daarbij ben je in staat om de klantverwachtingen helder te analyseren, te managen en actief bij te sturen waar nodig; · Je beheerst de Nederlandse en Engelse taal uitstekend in woord en geschrift; · Jouw persoonlijkheid kenmerkt zich door: gestructureerd, motiverend, communicatief sterk, duidelijk, open, tikje eigenwijs, enthousiast, relativerend, creatief en pragmatisch; · Je haalt energie uit het opstellen en bewaken van planningen, analyseren van gegevens en opstellen van duidelijke, gestructureerde rapportages en presentaties; · Je hebt minimaal een afgeronde bachelor, bij voorkeur richting bedrijfskunde, bedrijfseconomie en/of informatica. Wat bieden wij jou? Naast de genoemde leuke functie binnen een groeiend en innovatief bedrijf bieden wij: · Salaris : We bieden je een salaris tussen € 5.590 en € 7.958 per maand (o.b.v. 40 uur per week), afhankelijk van je ervaring en kennis; · Middelen : Leaseauto, laptop, telefoon; · Werkdagen : Je bent minimaal 4 dagen per week beschikbaar, al heeft 5 dagen onze voorkeur; · Vergoeding voor thuiswerken : Je kunt gedeeltelijk thuiswerken en krijgt een onkostenvergoeding van € 2,40 per thuiswerkdag. Ook krijg je een budget van € 750,- om thuis een ergonomische werkplek in te richten; · Workation : Je kunt tot 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar vanuit het buitenland werken; · Leuke teamactiviteiten : Leer je collega’s beter kennen door deel te nemen aan maandelijkse evenementen georganiseerd door ons energieke Fun-team, zoals een pubquiz, Zomer BBQ, wine & beer tastings en movie night; · Vakantiedagen : Je krijgt 25 vakantiedagen en de mogelijkheid om maximaal 20 extra dagen bij te kopen; · Groei en ontwikkelin g: De mogelijkheid om je vaardigheden en verantwoordelijkheden te ontwikkelen binnen de functie, middels opleidingen en Linkedin learning, of door te stromen naar een van de andere functies binnen CCS; · Vakantiegeld : Jaarlijks 8,33%; · Voordelen : Je krijgt een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling met een lage eigen bijdrage en kunt gebruikmaken van collectieve verzekeringen met korting. Ook is er een bedrijfsfitnessregeling voor een gezonde levensstijl en een fietsregeling voor duurzaam vervoer. Waarom CCS? Omdat wij geloven dat werk meer is dan een baan. Het is een plek waar je jezelf kunt zijn, impact kunt maken en kunt groeien. Het is een omgeving waar je wordt geïnspireerd om het beste uit jezelf te halen en samen te werken aan een duurzame toekomst. Kom bij ons en ontdek wat er mogelijk is als je een carrière bouwt vol passie, plezier en betekenis. Jij bent de ontbrekende schakel in ons team. Word onderdeel van ons verhaal. 🚀 Find Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

title: Senior AWS Consultant
description: CloudNation helpt organisaties om het maximale uit de cloud te halen. We combineren diepgaande technische expertise met een pragmatische aanpak en bouwen samen met onze klanten aan schaalbare, veilige en toekomstbestendige oplossingen. We geloven in doen wat werkt: geen dikke rapporten, maar concrete oplossingen met zichtbare impact. Onze consultants staan midden in de uitvoering, werken nauw samen met klanten en zoeken continu naar manieren om te verbeteren en te innoveren met cloud en AI. Wat ga je doen? Als AWS Cloud Consultant sta je midden in de uitvoering: Je ontwikkelt cloudstrategieën en vertaalt businessdoelen naar concrete AWS-oplossingen, op basis van een grondige analyse van de bestaande IT-omgeving en het AWS Well-Architected Framework. Je onderzoekt samen met klanten waar AI echt waarde toevoegt, van slimme automatisering tot generatieve AI met Amazon Bedrock. Je neemt de rol van meewerkend voorman: je stuurt engineers aan en werkt zelf actief mee aan de implementatie van cloudoplossingen. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de delivery binnen scope, stelt een Work Breakdown Structure op en bewaakt samen met de projectmanager de voortgang, kwaliteit en planning. Je coacht en ontwikkelt je team volgens het ‘To do, To participate, To do it yourself’-principe. Je zorgt dat oplossingen schaalbaar, veilig en toekomstbestendig zijn en blijft na oplevering betrokken bij optimalisatie en doorontwikkeling. Over deze rol Dit is een senior rol met een duidelijke Customer Lead-overlay. Naast een sterke basis als AWS Cloud Consultant ben jij het vaste aanspreekpunt voor de klant en verantwoordelijk voor de waarde die we samen realiseren, over de hele lifecycle. Je combineert technische kennis met leiderschap, neemt teams en partners mee en vertaalt cloudmogelijkheden naar concrete impact. Tegelijk bouw je aan sterke, langdurige klantrelaties en help je zowel de klant als het team steeds een stap verder. Als Customer Lead: Ben je het vaste aanspreekpunt en escalatiepunt voor de klant. Neem je eigenaarschap over de klantroadmap en stuur je op bedrijfswaarde. Ben je verantwoordelijk voor de uitkomsten van de delivery en stuur je bij wanneer resultaten afwijken van de verwachtingen. Vorm je tijdens Continuous Delivery samen met de People & Process Officer het governance-model richting de klant. Vertegenwoordig je intern het perspectief van de klant en breng je collega’s en partners op één lijn. Signaleer je kansen om de samenwerking verder uit te bouwen. Onze gedachte We werken volgens ons 6D Delivery Model. Als Customer Lead houd je de rode draad vast over alle fasen. Het zwaartepunt van jouw deliverywerk ligt hier: DISCOVER, DEFINE & DESIGN Je analyseert IT-omgevingen, voert Well-Architected Reviews uit en vertaalt businessdoelen naar concrete AWS-strategieën, migratieplannen, roadmaps en toekomstbestendige oplossingen. DEVELOP & DEPLOY Als meewerkend voorman stuur je engineers aan en werk je zelf mee aan de implementatie en uitrol. Je bewaakt scope, voortgang en kwaliteit, stelt de Work Breakdown Structure op en neemt eigenaarschap over de delivery, in nauwe afstemming met de klant en projectmanager. CONTINUOUS DELIVERY Je zorgt voor een succesvolle oplevering en blijft betrokken bij optimalisatie, innovatie en doorontwikkeling. In deze fase komt de Customer Lead-rol het sterkst naar voren: je bewaakt de klantwaarde en geeft samen met de People & Process Officer richting aan de governance. Wat neem je mee? Ruime ervaring, doorgaans 5+ jaar, met AWS-services, architectuur en cloudoplossingen. Ervaring met AWS-frameworks zoals Well-Architected, AWS CAF en landing zones, inclusief migraties en optimalisatie. Sterke hands-on ervaring met Infrastructure-as-Code, CI/CD en het realiseren van AWS-oplossingen. Ervaring met het aansturen van technische teams en het nemen van eigenaarschap over complexe klantprojecten. Je combineert technische expertise met sterk stakeholdermanagement en stuurt op bedrijfswaarde en resultaat. Ervaring met AI-assisted development en AI in je dagelijkse werk, bij voorkeur met een agentic way of working. Goede beheersing van Nederlands en Engels. Relevante AWS-certificeringen zijn een pré. Wat bieden wij? Een marktconform salaris van 66k-115k per jaar. Een leaseauto of mobiliteitsbudget, laptop, telefoon, pensioenregeling en 26 vakantiedagen. Een persoonlijk opleidings- en certificeringsbudget voor jouw ontwikkeling in AWS en AI. Ondersteuning bij het behalen van certificeringen, waarbij behaalde certificeringen terugkomen in je salaris. Een rol met veel eigenaarschap, waarin je een eigen klantportfolio draagt en stuurt op waarde en groei. Volop ruimte voor innovatie, eigen initiatief en het werken met de nieuwste cloud- en AI-technologie. Hybride werken, met Bunnik als thuisbasis en vrijdag als gezamenlijke kantoordag. Een open en ondernemende cultuur waarin we samenwerken, van elkaar leren en successen vieren. Over CloudNation CloudNation, an IG&H company, helpt organisaties versnellen met cloud en AI. Als AWS Premier Tier Services Partner combineren we diepgaande technische expertise met strategisch inzicht om organisaties niet alleen te moderniseren, maar ook toekomstbestendig te maken. We geloven dat echte impact ontstaat wanneer strategie en uitvoering samenkomen. Daarom adviseren onze consultants niet alleen, maar bouwen en realiseren ze ook: van de eerste strategie tot implementatie, optimalisatie en doorontwikkeling. AI? Wij maken het werkend. We geloven in AI voorbij de hype. We bouwen het, passen het toe bij klanten én gebruiken het iedere dag zelf.
